topic: Skipping rope: go easy on your calves and shins

slides.headline: Picked up the skipping rope again?
slides.sub: Skipping is great cardio. Here's how to keep calves and shins happy.

slides.title: Why skipping loads your legs
slides.body: Every jump asks your calves, Achilles and shins to absorb and push off. Hundreds of jumps add up quickly, especially if your legs aren't used to it.

slides.title: Start with short rounds
slides.body: Try 30 seconds on, 30 seconds off for five to ten minutes. Add a little time each week rather than jumping straight into long sessions your legs aren't ready for.

slides.title: Keep jumps low and soft
slides.body: Aim for small, quiet jumps on the balls of your feet with soft knees. You only need to clear the rope by a couple of centimetres.

slides.title: Surface and shoes matter
slides.body: A gym floor, wooden deck or mat is kinder than concrete. Supportive trainers help too. Add slow calf raises twice a week to build capacity in your calves and Achilles.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain in one spot on the shin, pain that's worse each session, pain at rest or at night, or swelling around the Achilles is worth an assessment.

slides.headline: Want to skip without the soreness?

caption:
Picked up the skipping rope for summer fitness? Your calves might be feeling it.

Skipping is quick, effective cardio, but every jump loads your calves, Achilles and shins. Sore legs usually mean you've done too much too soon, not that skipping is bad for you.

Start with short rounds, keep your jumps low and soft, choose a gym floor or mat over concrete, and add calf raises twice a week. Pain in one spot on the shin, pain at rest or at night, or a swollen Achilles is worth getting checked.
